sections.what_happened: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM -- Saudi-led coalition, via spokesman Turki al-Malki on X, carried by Reuters (T1), Al Jazeera liveblog (T2), Gulf Times (T3), Arab News (T3), Anadolu (T3), Al Arabiya (T3)] Air defence intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by Ansar Allah (the Ansar Allah) toward the Medina region, home to Islam's second-holiest city. The coalition statement referred to the wider Medina region and did not specify whether the missile was headed toward the city itself, and gave no details of the intended target or any damage. [VERIFIED FACT -- Reuters, Nov 5] Saudi civil defence issued a danger alert for Yanbu Governorate (Red Sea oil export hub; terminus of the East-West Pipeline that lets Saudi oil bypass the blockaded Strait of Hormuz, per Gulf Times) and emergency alerts for Sharurah in the southeast bordering Yemen; it was unclear if the Yanbu warning and the interception were connected. [VERIFIED FACT -- Reuters, Nov 5] Ansar Allah had yet to claim any attack on the kingdom on Thursday. [ATTRIBUTED REPORT -- Reuters, Nov 5] Ansar Allah said on Wednesday it had attacked Riyadh's international airport while Syria's President Ahmed al-Sharaa visited the kingdom; Saudi authorities have not confirmed that attack. [COUNTERPOINT -- on record] Ansar Allah has repeatedly said its forces would not target the holy cities of Mecca or Medina, and its attacks remain focused on Saudi energy and military infrastructure; on Oct 30 the coalition reported intercepting Ansar Allah drones in both the Medina and Mecca regions (Al Arabiya). [ATTRIBUTED, UNVERIFIED -- Times of Israel liveblog citing the Wall Street Journal] Ansar Allah is demanding $51 billion from Saudi Arabia to cease its attacks and wants Riyadh to recognise it as the legitimate ruler of Yemen; no WSJ text was surfaced in this scan and the figure is NOT independently verified — do not headline it. [CONTEXT -- 1300-06] This follows the Nov 4 Ansar Allah claims (missiles toward Najran, Jizan, King Khalid Airport; six ballistic missiles at al-Jawf/Lahij) which Riyadh has still not confirmed; the Medina-region launch is a NEW target and a NEW day, not a confirmation of the Nov 4 claims.
sections.what_verified: 6 distinct publisher families carry the coalition's statement: Reuters (T1) for the interception + Yanbu/Sharurah alerts + Riyadh-airport claim context; Al Jazeera liveblog (T2) for the interception + Yanbu alert; Gulf Times (T3); Arab News (T3); Anadolu (T3); Al Arabiya (T3). All six report the same primary source (the coalition's own statement); the underlying launch/interception rests on the coalition alone, so primary_source_single_family is true.
sections.what_disputed: Ansar Allah has not claimed the Thursday attack; the group has repeatedly denied targeting Mecca or Medina and says its attacks focus on energy and military infrastructure. The coalition gave no launch time, impact point, debris evidence or interceptor detail. The Nov 4 Ansar Allah claims (Najran/Jizan/King Khalid Airport, Riyadh airport) remain unconfirmed by Riyadh. The $51bn ceasefire-demand figure rests on a single liveblog citing the WSJ with no surfaced text.
sections.why_matters: LEAD. A ballistic missile fired at the region of Islam's second-holiest city — intercepted, says the Saudi coalition — on the same day Riyadh warned of danger at Yanbu, the Red Sea hub that lets Saudi oil bypass the blockaded Strait of Hormuz. Frame as an attributed coalition report with the Ansar Allah denial as the counterpoint; the moment is al-Malki's X post. Hard number in the title: 1 missile, 1 interception, 0 impacts (coalition claim).
sections.context: Background: Saudi-led coalition says it intercepted an Ansar Allah ballistic missile fired toward the Medina region; civil-defence alerts in Yanbu and Sharurah; Ansar Allah has not claimed the Thursday attack; Reuters reports Ansar Allah claimed on Wednesday it attacked Riyadh airport (unconfirmed by Riyadh)

totw_analysis: Our read: LEAD. A ballistic missile fired at the region of Islam's second-holiest city — intercepted, says the Saudi coalition — on the same day Riyadh warned of danger at Yanbu, the Red Sea hub that lets Saudi oil bypass the blockaded Strait of Hormuz. Frame as an attributed coalition report with the Ansar Allah denial as the counterpoint; the moment is al-Malki's X post. Hard number in the title: 1 missile, 1 interception, 0 impacts (coalition claim). The fault line our audience is arguing over: Holy city targeted or holy city protected? Ansar Allah has repeatedly denied aiming at Mecca or Medina, yet the coalition says a ballistic missile was fired at the Medina region and destroyed. Was this a deliberate strike on a holy city, a missile aimed at Yanbu and the oil-bypass pipeline that crossed Medina-region airspace, or a claim that cannot be tested?
